intro:
This file answers three questions about the SystemVerilog tier of lean-surfaces (ls-sv): **what does it refuse today**,
**what is meant to be allowed later (and what has to exist first)**, and **what will never be allowed (and which principle says so)**.

It is generated from [`docs/sv-refusals.json`](sv-refusals.json) by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and checked against the code by
`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check`: a tagged refusal in the extractor or the Lean code that is missing from the data, or a
listed tag that has disappeared from the code, fails the check. The svGolf-facing twin, for contestants and task authors, is
`svgolf/REFUSALS.md`, generated from the same data. It lives with the svGolf project (the golf branch), so the paths under `svgolf/`
cited in this file are absent from a checkout without it.

A refusal is a LOUD `Unsupported` node (extractor) or a loud process / expression / elaboration error (Lean) or a loader gate: the
design either loads with a defined meaning or it does not load. Nothing here is silently approximated. The long reasons live in the
per-topic documents linked at the end (`docs/sv-*.md`); this register is the index and the classification.
scope_note:
The register classifies each refusal for the **ls-sv semantics tier** (the `category` of the row). The charter rules the tier's endgame to be
the whole specification, including the verification tier (classes, constrained randomization, assertions) and the full clause-4 scheduler
([docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) sections 6.3, 6.4, 6.6), so a construct can be `later` for ls-sv and still be unacceptable in a
**svGolf submission**, whose scored artifact is a combinational Yosys netlist. Where the two differ the row carries a second line
`svGolf: ...` (the field `svgolf` in the data). Delays, randomness, classes, strings and reals are the typical cases: `later` in the
semantics, `never` for a golf submission (principles `P-NO-TIME`, `P-SYNTHESIZABLE`).

categories.refused-now: refused loudly today and this is the intended behaviour at this version; no future is recorded
categories.later: refused today and intended to be ALLOWED once a stated prerequisite is met (a proof obligation, a model extension, a checker stage, a measured benefit); the row names the prerequisite and, where recorded, the plan item
categories.never: refused by principle and not to be allowed: no meaning can be given that is the same for the proof (ls-sv / slang) and the score (Yosys netlist), or it is not synthesizable hardware, or it would let the proved design differ from the scored one; the row names the principle
categories.refused-pending: decided and in flight, not yet in the code (transitional): the row names the decision; the completeness check allows its tag to be absent and warns once it appears

principles.text: Proof and score read ONE program: a construct the two frontends (slang for the proof, Yosys for the score) read differently, that slang rejects (Thomas, 2026-10-31: "a good reason to reject"), or that Yosys cannot read, cannot be admitted.
No construct whose meaning is a synthesis-tool directive: pragmas, attributes, `ifdef SYNTHESIS / YOSYS, translate_off comments.
No delays, timing, wall-clock or time-dependent behaviour in a combinational task: synthesis ignores them, so the proved (timed) behaviour and the scored netlist would differ.

Not synthesizable hardware, for a design task whose scored artifact is a gate netlist from Yosys `read_verilog -sv`: class declarations, dynamic memory (queues, dynamic and associative arrays), `string` variables and parameters, `real` variables, fork/join, program blocks. The frontend does not read them (measured by `harness/sv/tools_split_audit/yosys_frontend.py`; a constant `real` in a parameter expression IS read), so they are out of scope for now; revisit if a different synthesis frontend is adopted (Thomas, 2026-10-31, about classes: a future internal synthesis frontend may change that). Host access (file I/O, system calls, DPI) is refused by its own policy, not by this principle.

The PIPELINE tools split (slang / ls-sv for the proof, Yosys for the score, Verilator and Xcelium as simulators give different values for the same text) and no consistent reading exists: refuse loudly, never decide for one side. A split in which only Icarus differs is not a refusal but a declared departure (Thomas, 2026-10-31), and neither is one in which only Xcelium differs from LRM text that slang, Verilator and Yosys follow (Thomas, 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f`).

A combinational result must be a function of the inputs, whatever the schedule: randomness is refused, and so is a design with no completed run (it never satisfies `Terminates2`). Where the LRM itself leaves the schedule open (IEEE 4.7) Thomas's ruling of 2026-10-31 is that the construct is to be modelled and the golfer proves the output the same in every legal run, not that it is refused for that reason. A simulator-versus-synthesizer mismatch (self-reading `always_comb`: the LRM's answer is deterministic, the synthesizers compute another) is not that case.

(added by the register authors, to confirm) The evidence a verdict rests on (checker, trusted statement, generated Goal, axiom set, toolchain) must not be changeable by the submission; a proof is accepted by the kernel from the allowed axioms alone.

(Thomas, 2026-10-31 for the READING of files; confirmed 2026-11-01 for the rest of the family: "Yes, don't allow this. It's not safe.") The SystemVerilog text of a submission cannot read or write host files, run programs, read the environment or call native code: the checker runs untrusted text on the organizer's machine (Yosys's read_verilog itself opens the file of a $readmemh). The Lean file of a submission is not scanned for it: it is CONTAINED, by the checker's sandbox around every process that runs submitted text (WP-S, 2026-10-31; known hole "Host access from the Lean file of a submission", mitigated).

policies.policy: If slang reports a program illegal, that is a good reason to reject it. LRM = the IEEE 1800 Language Reference Manual; the register cites the clause where there is one.
policies.source: Thomas 2026-10-31 (rulings on the register's never rows); docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md

policies.policy: "slang reports a program illegal" means (Thomas 2026-11-01: yes) the full slang driver, parse, elaboration AND ANALYSIS errors (`multiple-always-assigns`, `mixed-var-assigns`, "cannot assign to input port", "'always' procedure does not advance time"). IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-01 (WP-R-D). `Compilation.getAllDiagnostics()`, which the extractor, `fourstate` and `banlist` read, omits the analysis pass (`Driver.runAnalysis`, pyslang `analysis.AnalysisManager.analyze` on an elaborated compilation); three of its five errors (`MultipleAlwaysAssigns`, `MixedVarAssigns`, `MultipleContAssigns`) are WARNINGS by slang's own definition that the driver promotes to errors, so `Diagnostic.isError()` misses them too, and the classification asks the Driver's own DiagnosticEngine (default severities) with a NULL source location, so that no `pragma diagnostic` of the program can downgrade a report (stricter than the slang CLI). The extractor refuses with the kind `SlangAnalysis:<slang code>` and slang's message (a top without parameters: in the envelope; a top with parameters: per parameter point, the probe sidecar's `frontend_errors` and `frontend_analysis`, because an analysis error can depend on the point: sem2/drv_pw_ff is illegal at D = 2 and legal at D = 1); svGolf's `banlist` front check and `fourstate` stage refuse with `slang analysis error <code> at <file>:<line>: <message>` (svgolf/score/slangdriver.py). Until then the rule held for these shapes only through Yosys `check` (fourstate) and the Lean driver guards, and not at all for `initial` plus `always_comb`. IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-01 (WP-RB1) for the parse, preprocessor and elaboration errors of the symbolic compilation: the extractor carries each as `SlangError:<slang code>` (row sa-slang-error; same top-without-parameters / per-point split), so an envelope of an illegal program is loud, where before it was identical to the legal program's. Still outside (see `holes`): the elaboration warnings the driver also promotes (`IndexOOB`, `RangeOOB`, ...), a task with an empty banlist (no banlist front check), and the extractor's M0 single-file mode.
policies.source: docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md section 5 (findings 2 and 6); adversarial review 2026-10-31; extractors/sv/test_slang_analysis.py; svgolf/score/slangdriver.py; WP-RB1 (svgolf/design/real-world-sv/rb0/ENVELOPE-ERRORS.md; extractors/sv/test_slang_errors.py)

The same holds, since 2026-11-01, where only Xcelium differs from LRM text that slang, Verilator and Yosys follow.

policies.policy: File reading is disallowed in the SystemVerilog text of a submission: no construct that makes the checker read a host file ($readmemh, $readmemb, and the file-reading tasks of LRM 21.3 such as $fopen for reading, $fscanf, $fgets, $fread). It is dangerous because Yosys's read_verilog opens the file of a $readmemh itself while it reads the design, on the organizer's machine, so a host file (a salt, an oracle) could be pulled into the netlist and leaked through the score.
policies.source: Thomas 2026-10-31 (rulings on the register's never rows: 'Stuff like reading files sounds dangerous. Maybe it's best to disallow those. Unless there are some very good reasons to keep them'; no good reason is known); svgolf/PLAN2.md

policies.policy: The rest of the host-access family follows the same principle in the SystemVerilog text: no construct that WRITES a host file ($writememh, $writememb, $fdisplay*, $fwrite*, ...), runs a program ($system), reads the environment or command line ($test$plusargs, $value$plusargs, $getenv), writes a dump, coverage, SDF or Annex D file, or calls native code (DPI). Recorded as svGolf never rows (the rows beyond the memory-file and file I/O ones carry proposed = true). The Lean file of a submission is contained by the sandbox instead (next policy).
policies.source: Thomas 2026-11-01 ("Yes, don't allow this. It's not safe."), extending his 2026-10-31 file-reading ruling; svgolf/PLAN2.md

policies.policy: Host access from the Lean file of a submission (reading and writing host files, the network, other programs, the environment, signals to other processes) is disallowed by CONTAINMENT, not by scanning the Lean text: every process that runs submitted text (the Lean compiles, the comparator and leanchecker, the extractor, Yosys, Verilator and its C++ build, the compiled model, svgolf-eval) runs under the operating system's sandbox (macOS Seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap) with no network, reads only of its program, the toolchain, the Lean search path and its inputs, writes only of one fresh output directory, no other program, a scrubbed environment (the competition salt is invisible) and wall-clock, memory, output and file-size limits enforced from outside. `check.py --sandbox {off,auto,require}` (default auto); `leaderboard.py add`/`verify` and every competition run use `require`, so a record is made inside the sandbox or not at all. A scan of the Lean file is not the mechanism: the shipped references use a local `elab` and macros, Lean metaprograms reach IO under many names, and `unsafe` code makes the interpreter itself untrusted. A hostile file that catches its errors is accepted and neutralized (a denied call cannot be told from a permitted one); the residuals are listed in the known hole "Host access from the Lean file of a submission".
policies.source: Thomas 2026-10-31 (file reading and similar host access are dangerous and to be disallowed) as implemented by WP-S (svgolf/check/sandbox/, svgolf/README.md "Sandbox"); the choice of containment over a Lean-side gate was the register authors', signed off by Thomas 2026-11-01 ("sounds good")

policies.policy: An Xcelium-only dissent is NOT a tools split: when the LRM text agrees with Verilator, slang and Yosys and only Xcelium differs, the construct is admitted and Xcelium is a declared departure (a hash-bound `oracle_disagreement` row). This supersedes the Xcelium clause of the 2026-10-29 policy ("where Xcelium departs from explicit LRM text and the others follow it, refuse"). Consequences recorded 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f` in string literals (row `lit-string`) are to be admitted; `\xHH` (row `lit-string-hex`) stays refused because Yosys, which produces the scored netlist, reads it differently from slang and the LRM (a proof/score split, not an Xcelium dissent); `pr-init-var` stays refused until the sequential tier because the LRM does not say whether an initializer is another process (Verilator warns citing IEEE 9.2.2.2, Xcelium rejects). IMPLEMENTED 2026-11-01 (WP-R-D): `\a \v \f` are admitted by the extractor (`_disputed_string_escape` now reads only the hex escape); rows `lit_str_ctl` (Xcelium declared departure `xcelium-named-control-escape-letters`, XREF-DECLARED) and `lit_str_ctl_ok` (the agreeing spellings, XREF-MATCH) of harness/sv/cases2.json; the Xcelium pins are in harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json. Not touched: `lit-string-hex` (stays refused) and `pr-init-var` (stays refused).
policies.source: Thomas 2026-11-01 ("This could be an Xcelium bug. You should check the spec. If the sv spec agrees with verilator, slang and yosys, we'll accept it."; `\xHH`: "You decide"); docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md sections 5 and 6; docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md, 'String literal escapes `\a \v \f`'

policies.policy: `bv_decide` is NOT SUPPORTED in svGolf submissions for now: it runs an external SAT solver (the toolchain's `cadical`), and the checker does not support external solvers. Allowing it would need the solution's compile sandbox to grant `fork`, the exec of `cadical` and a writable temporary directory (WP-BV measured that these three are the minimum), a widening Thomas declined (it also lets a hostile file start further copies of `lean`, bounded only by the supervisor's memory and wall limits). So `allow_bv_decide: true` in a `task.json` is an infrastructure error, `check.py` never passes `--bv-decide`, the sandbox Spec never gets the solver (one constant, `BV_DECIDE_SUPPORTED = False` in `check.py`, that no environment variable, option or task key reads), the comparator rejects a `bv_decide` axiom naming this policy, and a failed `bv_decide` proof carries a hint (use `decide +kernel`, `omega`, `simp` or a symbolic argument). The earlier 2026-11-01 ruling ("we should remove the bitblast ban") stands as the intent for a checker that has a solver sandbox: the comparator's re-verification of the generated axiom (it decodes `E` from its kernel value, requires the toolchain's `toExpr` of it to equal that value, and evaluates `verifyBVExpr E C`) and the sandbox grant are kept, dormant, with tests; enabling is a constant, the sign-off and the checklist in `svgolf/README.md` "`bv_decide`". Submissions still cannot declare axioms of their own; `native_decide`, `decide +native`, `Lean.ofReduceBool`, `extern` and `implemented_by` stay refused. Fixed-size subgoals only, when it is enabled: a proof for all N still needs a symbolic argument.
policies.source: Thomas 2026-11-01, after the sandbox widening was explained to him ("maybe that's a bad idea. Let's not support external solvers for now"); earlier the same day: "we should remove the bitblast ban, since we have the proof time limit anyway", "Submissions shouldn't be allowed to declare new axioms"; svgolf/README.md "`bv_decide`"; svgolf/design/bv-decide/NOTE.md; rows sg-bv-decide, sg-extern

policies.policy: Mathlib in submissions keeps the wide import roots (`Mathlib`, `Batteries`, `Aesop`, `Qq`, `ProofWidgets`, `Plausible`, `ImportGraph`, `LeanSearchClient`): the common libraries are to be available, so a whole-library `import Mathlib` has to load on the organizer's machine.
policies.source: Thomas 2026-11-01 ("Sure, let's make the common libraries available"); svgolf/README.md "Mathlib in submissions"

holes.name: slang's driver: what the analysis-pass rule still does not read
holes.text: The analysis-pass errors (`multiple-always-assigns`, `mixed-var-assigns`, `multiple-cont-assigns`, "cannot assign to input port", "'always' procedure does not advance time") ARE read since 2026-11-01 (policy "slang reports a program illegal"). What it does not read, measured on the committed corpora with the Driver's own severities: (1) the elaboration-time warnings that the driver promotes to errors (`IndexOOB`, `RangeOOB`, `DynamicNotProcedural`, `UnknownSystemName`, ...: 175 diagnostic codes have another severity in the Driver's engine than in a bare DiagnosticEngine, 41 of them promoted from warning to error and 134 switched off): they are NOT errors for the extractor, because 9 envelopes with `IndexOOB`, 9 with `RangeOOB` and 1 with `DynamicNotProcedural` (of the 1271 committed envelopes) are admitted differential rows that read x for the out-of-range select, Xcelium-pinned; for svGolf `fourstate`'s rule (c) already refuses the out-of-range ones as x sources, and the 4 svGolf corpus files with such a code (const_oob_write, param_oob, unique_rare, host_dump) are refused by other rules; promoting them is a policy choice, not a measurement; (2) the extractor's M0 single-file mode (`process_file`, sv-0.1): 3 committed M0 envelopes hold an analysis error (always_comb_written_excluded, always_no_control_refuse, multiple_variable_continuous_drivers) and are conformance-lane designs, untouched; (3) a parametric top's default-point envelope carries no analysis marker, and since WP-RB1 no `SlangError` marker when `--probe-points` was given (the verdict is per point, the probe sidecar), so a consumer that instantiates a parametric envelope at a point no sidecar covers relies on the Lean `driversOk` guard (svGolf always probes the scoring point); (4) a task with an EMPTY banlist skips the banlist front check (`banlist.check` returns early), so `fourstate` is the only svGolf stage that reads slang's analysis errors there; (5) `srcgate.py` parses without elaborating and has no analysis to read; (6) the analysis reads the design's own hierarchy, as the other stages do: an uninstantiated module with an analysis error is not refused (the slang CLI would); parse and elaboration errors, by contrast, are read over the whole compilation since WP-RB1 (row sa-slang-error), an uninstantiated module's undeclared name included.
holes.source: docs/sv-tools-split-audit.md section 5; svgolf/score/slangdriver.py; extractors/sv/test_slang_analysis.py; measured by WP-R-D 2026-11-01 (harness: scratchpad measure.py over Examples/system-verilog and svgolf); extractors/sv/test_slang_errors.py

holes.name: Host access from the Lean file of a submission (svGolf)
holes.text: MITIGATED by the checker's sandbox (WP-S, 2026-10-31); not gated. The source gate's host-access rule (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`) covers the SystemVerilog text. A Solution.lean is compiled and elaborated with the checker's privileges and `import Lean` (since WP-B, Mathlib) is allowed: before the sandbox, a reference solution with an added `#eval IO.FS.readFile "/etc/hosts"` and an `IO.FS.writeFile` was ACCEPTED (stage done), read the file, wrote another one, and what the `#eval` printed came back in `stages.solution.messages`; the same file read the competition salt `SVGOLF_POSTSYNTH_SALT` out of the checker's environment (with it a player precomputes the post-synthesis vectors), opened a TCP connection (Lean core has sockets, no program is spawned), replaced the trusted `Design.olean` through a hard link and spawned `/bin/sh`. A scan of the Lean file cannot stop that (the shipped references use a local `elab` and macros; Lean metaprograms reach IO under many names; `unsafe` code makes the interpreter untrusted). The mitigation is a sandbox around every process that runs submitted text: `check.py --sandbox {off,auto,require}` (default auto; `leaderboard.py add`/`verify` use `require`), macOS Seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap, a canary self-test at every start, no network, reads only of the inputs, writes only of one fresh output directory, no other program, a scrubbed environment, limits enforced from outside; tests/run.py step `sandbox` pins the attacks. RESIDUAL: (1) on a machine without a mechanism `auto` runs unsandboxed and says so (`require` refuses); (2) a hostile file that catches its errors is accepted, neutralized; (3) the existence, size and times of any path are visible (global file-read-metadata, for speed); (4) the parsers that run in the checker's own process (pyslang in the source gate, the banlist and fourstate front checks) are not sandboxed: moving them into one sandboxed worker is the recorded next step; (5) a crafted .olean is loaded by the comparator and leanchecker, which also run inside the sandbox, with the kernel replay as the check; (6) kernel and Seatbelt bugs, what system.sb grants every Apple command-line program; (7) Linux was validated at the self-test and process level (Rocky 9.8, bwrap 0.6.3), not yet with Lean.
holes.source: svgolf/README.md Sandbox and Checker v0 limits; svgolf/check/sandbox/; measured by the register authors and by WP-S

schema: entries[] (ls-sv tier) and svgolf.entries[] (svGolf checker) share one record shape:

id (unique slug), tag (display name; `Family:detail` where the code has one), group, layers (extractor | lean-model | lean-guard | lean-loader | lean-proof-tooling | svgolf-*), trigger (a measured source, `H:` = the body of the standard test module), why, category (refused-now | later | never | refused-pending), proposed (true = not confirmed by Thomas), decided_by (the recorded decision), since (date, when known).

later: prerequisite (required) and plan (a plan_items id); never: principle (required, from the principle table); refused-pending: decided_by or source (the decision) and kinds that may be absent from the code.
svgolf (optional, on an ls-sv entry): {category, principle | prerequisite, proposed}: the status for a svGolf submission when it differs from the ls-sv status.

kinds.extractor / kinds.lean: the code tags the row covers (exact strings; `glob:<pattern>` for a deliberate family; `@default:<function>` for an extractor site that takes the slang class name; a bare `*` for a site whose whole kind is built at run time). The completeness check requires every live code tag to be covered and every listed tag to exist.

match: [{file, text}]: for a refusal that has only a message, the text must still be found in the file. where: [{file, fn}]: the function that raises it (line numbers are resolved by --where, never stored). attacks: svgolf only, `task/name` of every tests/expected.json design the row explains.

evidence (where it is documented), unverified (read from the source, never triggered by a run), verified_by_run, notes, value_rank / value_note (the ordering of the 'Allowed later' table), aggregate (svGolf only: a summary row hidden from svgolf/REFUSALS.md).

entries.trigger: H: always_comb begin y=0; for (int i=0;i<4;i++) y[i]=a[i]; end
entries.why: Literal-bounded, source-pure single-iterator forms are unrolled in the extractor; parameter-dependent pure bounds and positive compound steps (literal or parameter-valued) are retained and expanded at each instantiation point. A comparison whose operands are not both signed `int`-class values is loud until the loop evaluator carries SystemVerilog's real comparison signedness. Effectful, multi-iterator, overflowing, and otherwise nonliteral forms remain loud.
entries.prerequisite: remaining prerequisite: broader loop state for effectful or nonliteral bounds
entries.evidence: svgolf/tests/_example/attacks/README.md (for_counter_*); svgolf/PLAN.md task ladder; docs/sv-loops.md (M0 tier); 11 svgolf/score/tests/*.sv; Examples/system-verilog/sem2/always_ff_loop
entries.value_note: popcount, carry chains and parity trees written as loops (task ladder: popcount)
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: approved the refused-now and later classifications of the register
entries.notes: Since 2026-11-01 (WP-PROC X1) the unroll also takes an iterator declared OUTSIDE the header (`integer i; for (i = 0; ...)`) when every reference to it lies inside loops that iterate it (the declaration is then dead and erased; `int`/`integer` only, not a port), the steps `i += c` / `i -= c`, and the comparisons `<=` / `>=` (`LessThanEqual`/`GreaterThanEqual` were missing from the operator table). Rows `proc_loop_forms`, `proc_loop_forms_local`, `proc_loop_forms2`. Since 2026-11-02 (parameter-point procedural loops), a positive parameter expression is also accepted as a compound step and evaluated at each point (`symbolic_parameter_for_parameter_step`), and an external iterator with a parameter bound is retained as the same point-expanded loop (`symbolic_parameter_for_external`). Since 2026-11-04, mixed signed/unsigned loop comparisons are refused (`loop_mixed_signed_refuse`, `loop_mixed_signed_param_refuse`) rather than using Python signed ordering. Retained loops whose user-function body reads a same-named module/local parameter are also refused (`loop_name_capture_refuse`) until iterator bindings are separate from `ParamRef` lookup. Header iterators other than signed 32-bit `int`/`integer` are refused (`loop_typed_iterator_refuse`) until declared-width wrapping and termination are modeled. Effectful headers and iterators observed outside their loops stay loud. The same literal unroll is exercised inside a retained timed always_ff process by always_ff_loop.

entries.trigger: H: assign (strong0, highz1) y = a;  /  assign (weak0, weak1) y = a;
entries.why: A drive strength on a continuous assignment has no reading the tools share. Yosys 0.53 cannot read it at all (`read_verilog -sv`: syntax error, so the scored netlist does not exist); Icarus 12 applies it (a highz term drives z); Xcelium 24.03 ignores it on a variable (`*W,CAVSTR`, y = a); Verilator 5.042 accepts a strength without a high-impedance term and stops on `highz` (`Unsupported: highz strength`). The symbolic extractor used to admit it as a plain assignment, because `_continuous_assignment_has_strength` reads source bytes that only the M0 path loads (the M0 path keeps its own handling). The rule is the syntactic one: every strength-qualified `assign` is refused, taken from the syntax tree (`lower_proc.has_strength`); nets with a strength were already refused (`NetSymbol:net-z`, N2).
entries.evidence: rows cstr_highz and cstr_weak (measured field: Icarus, Xcelium, Yosys, Verilator, 2026-11-01); extractors/sv/test_continuous_strength.py
entries.notes: WP-PROC follow-up 1 (2026-11-01). Proposed `never` (P-SAME-PROGRAM: the scoring frontend cannot read the text); the alternative is `later` if Yosys gains the syntax. Nothing in the surveyed corpora (216 real files, 82 RB0 blocks, 240 probes) writes a strength.

A block that fails keeps this tag with the rule in its text.

It stays loud in a parameter default, a localparam or a generate condition: the constant tier has its own width rules for `~` (an INT-class `~` is refused there) and the lowering was not measured against them.

The departure is DECLARED (rows `lit_str_ctl`, declaration `xcelium-named-control-escape-letters`; control row `lit_str_ctl_ok`), not refused. entries.tag: PortConn:driver (clause 4: two always blocks writing one bit)
entries.trigger: always_comb y[0]=a; always_comb y[0]=b;
entries.why: IEEE 9.2.2.2 and 9.2.2.4: the variables an always_comb / always_ff writes shall not be assigned by any other process (an `initial` block and a plain `always` are processes too). slang reports an ERROR (multiple-always-assigns) for two always_comb or two always_ff writers of one bit, and for one of them plus any other process; Xcelium rejects (MULAXX); Icarus runs it and keeps the first block's value, Verilator warns, Yosys warns of conflicting drivers. A program slang rejects is rejected. Conservatively over-refuses a plain `always @(posedge clk or negedge rn)` that shares a bit with another process (`alwaysFFR` counts as exclusive, Hier2.lean `Process2.exclusive`); the single-process form is not refused (drv_pw_plain_always).

Thomas's slang ruling of 2026-11-01 covers the analysis-pass errors, and it is implemented (row sa-slang-analysis: the extractor refuses a parameter-free top on slang's `MultipleAlwaysAssigns`, per point for a top with parameters; the Lean `driversOk` guard stays verified by the parametric twins drv_pw_lit_p, drv_genvar_ov_p and by drv_pw_ff, drv_pw_gv). Two PLAIN `always @*` writers of one bit are a different case: legal text, slang-clean, and a genuine race (Icarus, Verilator, the Yosys netlist and Xcelium give four different traces on the audit probe two_plain), so by the nondeterminism ruling the construct is in principle one to model; today nothing admits it, because the extractor refuses `always @*` (`TimedStatement:ImplicitEventControl`) and svGolf's fourstate rejects it (Yosys `check`: multiple conflicting drivers). The `initial` plus `always_comb` pair (init_comb_proc) was a slang error that the extractor and fourstate admitted and that run2 refused only because the loader has no `Initial` process kind; since 2026-11-01 slang's report refuses it in the extractor and in svGolf's banlist and fourstate stages (rows sa_initial_comb, slang_initial_comb), so admitting `initial` later does not reopen it.

entries.trigger: H: always_comb begin y = t; t = a; end   /   if (c) t = a; y = t; t = b;   (a bit read before it is written, written later)
entries.why: IEEE 9.2.2.2.1(b) leaves any expression the block itself writes out of its implicit sensitivity list, so the LRM's simulation answer for `y = t; t = a;` is deterministic: the block does not re-run on its own write of `t`, and `y` stays one change behind `a`. Icarus 12 and Xcelium 24.03 follow it; Verilator and the Yosys netlist give the settled value (`y = a`). The event-driven simulators and the synthesizers split, so the proof and the score would read different programs. This is NOT an Icarus-only split and NOT LRM nondeterminism.

entries.notes: Latches that never re-write the bits they read stay admitted. Recorded over-refusals: statically infeasible path combinations, dead reads, a run-time index read of a partly written signal. AUDIT 2026-10-31 (corrected after review), class (c): re-measured on all 9 rows (Xcelium = Icarus from cycle 1 on, `xx` at cycle 0; Verilator and the Yosys netlist settled). The first draft of the audit moved this row to `later` on the nondeterminism ruling; that was wrong. The LRM's answer is deterministic, so the ruling does not apply, and a run-set lift would be EMPTY for a genuine self-read: `CombTask.Computes` quantifies over every run, the stale run gives y_k = a_(k-1) where the task demands fn(a_k), so the theorem is unprovable; what a lift admits is only the over-refusal residue above, which a sharper guard admits for far less. The real question is Thomas's (NOTE question 1): which reading does the proof follow, the LRM's simulation (stale) or the synthesizers' (settled)? Following the synthesizers means departing from explicit LRM text for Icarus AND Xcelium, which the 2026-10-29 policy forbids unless he amends it. Not a candidate for `later` until he answers.

entries.trigger: H: assign w = t; always_comb begin y = w; t = a; end   (also assign chains, ~ and slice copies, port loops formed after flattening)
entries.why: An always_comb reads a bit downstream, through a continuous assign, of a bit it writes at or after the read: Icarus propagates the copy inside the block's run and loses the wake-up (y lags); Xcelium, Verilator, the Yosys netlist and the settle semantics defer it (y = a). Only Icarus differs; IEEE 4.7/4.8 (a procedural statement need not execute as one event, update events may be taken in any order) arguably make Icarus's order legal too.

entries.tag: run2: timeout (a combinational loop that never settles)
entries.trigger: assign a = en ? ~a : 1'b0;  (a true oscillator once en = 1: run2 answers timeout, no completed run)
entries.why: combSettle2 re-runs processes to a fixpoint within fuel; an oscillating loop has no completed run. Measured: a true oscillator hangs Icarus, aborts Verilator ("did not converge") and ends at an arbitrary value in Xcelium, so there is no value for the tools to agree on, and such a design can never satisfy `Terminates2`. A loop that SETTLES is not this row: run2 completes it (mux feedback, SR latch, a structural loop computing a = b = d, and `assign a = ~a`, which settles at x). Mux feedback and the structural loop give identical traces in all five tools; the NOR latch agrees except at the (1,1) then (0,0) transition, a genuine race on which Verilator and Xcelium end in different states and Icarus hangs.
entries.notes: AUDIT 2026-10-31 (corrected after review), class (d) in the narrow sense: no completed run, so there is nothing to lift. The first draft moved the row to `later` on the strength of the SETTLING loops, which run2 already admits: they are not an ls-sv refusal. They are refused downstream by svGolf's fourstate stage (Yosys `check`: found logic loop; svGolf rows sg-fs-conflict and sg-terminates), and that refusal is load-bearing: the probe loop_lat_if (`always_comb if (y) t = a; else t = 1'b0;` and `always_comb y = t;`, a loop that spans two blocks) runs in the model as the constant 0 (run2 on two stimuli; by hand for every stimulus: the start is x and `if (y)` takes the else branch), while the scored netlist is `y = y & a`, which holds state (two stable states at a = 1). Terminates2 and Computes do not reject it. See NOTE section 7.

svgolf.intro:
svGolf asks for two things about each design you submit: a Lean proof that it meets the task's trusted statement under the ls-sv
semantics, and a score from a pinned Yosys flow. The checker refuses a design or a proof when the proof and the score could be about
different circuits, or when the evidence could be forged. This document lists every refusal the checker makes, why, and what you
can write instead, then says which refusals are meant to go away and which never will.

It has two halves that are easy to confuse. **The checker's own stages** (source gate, banlist, fourstate, statement, axioms, score,
post-synthesis check) are described below stage by stage. **The language tier** (`ls-sv`, the semantics your proof is about) refuses
more constructs than the checker does; those show up as `extract` or `design` failures and are summarised near the end and listed in
full in `docs/sv-refusals.md` of the lean-surfaces repository.

This file is generated from `docs/sv-refusals.json` of lean-surfaces by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and is written to be read without
the rest of that repository: links to lean-surfaces documents are given as repository paths.

stages.refuses: unknown keys, a status other than ready / draft, a `ready` task without a reference proof

stages.what: checks the Lean file's imports against an allowlist
stages.refuses: any import outside Init, Std, Lean, LeanModels.Sv.*, SvGolf.*, tasks.*, Submission.Design and the Mathlib packages (Mathlib, Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient), read from the header as Lean reads it (a comment between two imports separates them) and checked again against the imports Lean recorded in the compiled solution; a second file; `module` / `prelude` headers; a module no package has a source for (a stale name) is a rejection, a package or module missing from the machine (not built, not on the search path, a checkout not at the pinned revision) is an infrastructure error

stages.what: `score/srcgate.py`: makes the proved program and the scored program ONE text and strips every comment
stages.refuses: preprocessor directives, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments, `unique` / `unique0` / `priority`, x/z/? literal digits, odd characters, host access (file, process, environment, dump and DPI constructs)

stages.what: the pinned lean-surfaces extractor reads the canonical text
stages.refuses: whatever the extractor refuses (the language tier), a wrong top module, a parameter list that differs from the task's

stages.what: `score/banlist.py`: pyslang front check plus a Yosys backstop
stages.refuses: the run-time operators the task bans, in every disguise Yosys turns into the same cell; for a task that bans an operator, also every error of slang's analysis pass (as `fourstate`)

any way an x or z value can arise: constants with unknown bits, out-of-range selects, undriven or conflicting nets, logic loops, latches, and every error of slang's analysis pass (two writers of one variable, mixed continuous and procedural assignment, writing an input port, an `always` without timing control)

stages.what: builds the trusted svGolf modules and the ls-sv evaluator (not timed)

stages.refuses: loader refusals: cross-checks against slang, the one-driver rule, self-reading `always_comb`, select guards, the multi-point probe check

stages.what: compiles `Solution.lean` under the task's time limit
stages.refuses: a proof that does not compile in time

stages.what: snapshots the trusted files before and after the solution builds
stages.refuses: a solution whose build changes a staged or trusted file (a tripwire, not a sandbox)
a missing theorem, a proof of another statement, axioms outside the task's set, `extern` / `implemented_by`

stages.what: kernel replay of the submission's modules
stages.refuses: declarations added with the kernel check switched off

stages.what: `score/score.py`: the two-stage Yosys + ABC flow and the GE table
stages.refuses: a netlist with cells the table does not price (latches, flip-flops), a non-deterministic flow, a design over the depth budget

stages.what: `check/postsynth.py`: ls-sv and the scored netlist (Verilator) must agree on every vector of the budget
stages.refuses: any disagreement, x/z in ls-sv outputs, a netlist Verilator will not build; a rejection is a bug report

policies: **Combinational tasks only for now.** Clocked designs, registers and pipelines are refused until the sequential layer exists (Thomas, 2026-10-29).

**Where the pipeline tools split, the design is refused**, never decided for one side: slang / ls-sv (the proof), Yosys (the score), Verilator and Xcelium are compared, and a shape they read differently is a loud refusal (Thomas). A difference that only Icarus shows is a declared departure, not a refusal (Thomas, 2026-10-31), and so is one that only Xcelium shows against LRM text the other tools follow (Thomas, 2026-11-01: `\a \v \f` are admitted).

**A program slang rejects is rejected, and LRM-legal nondeterminism is to be modelled rather than forbidden** (Thomas, 2026-10-31). No construct is admitted on the second ruling yet: the model does not exist, and the audit found that the rows it was first thought to cover are not LRM nondeterminism (self-reading `always_comb`: the LRM's answer is deterministic and the synthesizers compute another; settling combinational loops: refused by fourstate, and some hold state).

**Everything the proof and the score could read differently is refused exactly, before any proof is tried** (the x/z rules, the source gate), and the post-synthesis check is the backstop for the disagreements nobody has found.
**No other restrictions.** Beyond the per-task operator banlist and these safety gates, write any SystemVerilog ls-sv can load.
**Contestants may add features to ls-sv by pull request, and Thomas approves every such PR.** See 'How a refusal becomes allowed'.

**Proofs are symbolic and parametric** (for all N). `bv_decide` is not supported for now (it runs an external SAT solver, which the checker does not support: Thomas, 2026-11-01); `native_decide` is banned in submissions.

**No host access in the SystemVerilog text.** A submitted design cannot read host files (Thomas, 2026-10-31); by the same principle (proposed, to confirm) it cannot write them, run programs, read the environment, write dumps or call native code. The source gate refuses the constructs; the console tasks (`$display`, `$write`, `$finish`, ...) stay. The Lean file is not covered (see the limits).

groups.title: Stage `source`: one program for both tools
groups.intro: Yosys and slang (the frontend your proof is about) read the same file differently when it contains directives, attributes or pragma comments. The gate refuses those and hands every later stage one canonical text with all comments stripped. It also refuses every construct that reaches the machine the checker runs on (`$readmemh`, `$fopen`, `$system`, `$value$plusargs`, `$dumpfile`, DPI, ...): Yosys opens a `$readmemh` file itself while it reads the design.
groups.refused_example:
`ifdef SYNTHESIS
  assign y = a & b;     // Yosys defines SYNTHESIS, slang does not
`else
  assign y = a | b;
`endif
(* keep *) wire t;      // attribute: Yosys gives it a meaning
// synopsys translate_off
initial $readmemh("/etc/hosts", mem);   // host file: refused
initial $system("id");                 // host program: refused
import "DPI-C" function int c_fn(int x);   // native code: refused

groups.title: Stage `source` and `fourstate`: no x or z may arise
groups.intro: ls-sv computes with unknown values like an IEEE simulator; Yosys treats them as don't-cares. Wherever an x reaches a decision the proved and the scored circuits can differ, and you choose where. Every SOURCE of an x or z is refused, exactly. A `casez` item may use `z` and `?`, a `casex` item `x`, `z`, `?`.
groups.write_ok:
always_comb begin
  casez (a[1:0])
    2'b1?: y = 1'b1;     // wildcard digit in a casez item: allowed
    default: y = 1'b0;
  endcase
end
groups.refused_example:
assign y = a[0] ? 1'bz : a[1];     // z literal
localparam logic [1:0] K = 2'd1 / 2'd0;   // constant division by zero is x
logic [3:0] m; ... m[{1'b1, a[1:0]}]     // index can leave the range: x
logic u; assign y = u ? a : b;           // u is undriven

groups.title: Stage `banlist`: the task's banned operators
groups.intro: A task bans the run-time operator that IS the task, plus whatever Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc turns `+` and `-` chains into the cells of `*`). Constant arithmetic (parameters, genvar loops, index arithmetic over parameters and genvars) and comparisons stay allowed. Which operators are banned is per task: `add`, `mul` and `_example` ban `+ - * / % **`; `fdivp` bans `/ % **`.
groups.write_ok:
for (genvar i = 0; i < N; i++) begin : g
  assign s[i] = a[i] ^ b[i] ^ c[i];     // gates, not +
  assign c[i+1] = (a[i] & b[i]) | (c[i] & (a[i] ^ b[i]));   // i+1 is constant arithmetic
end
groups.refused_example:
assign s = a + b + cin;          // run-time + in a task that bans it
assign y = a * b;                // run-time *
assign n = $countones(a);        // Yosys builds it from $add cells
assign p = arr.sum();            // array reduction = run-time +

groups.title: Stages `extract` and `design`: the language tier and the parameter list
groups.intro: The proof is about what the pinned extractor and the ls-sv loader accept. A construct they refuse fails here with the tier's own message. The top module's overridable parameters must be exactly the task's, by name and order, because the scoring script overrides them by name.
groups.write_ok: module band #(parameter int N = 4)(input logic [N-1:0] a, b, output logic [N-1:0] y);
groups.refused_example:
module band #(parameter int N = 4, parameter int M = 2)(...);   // an extra parameter
module band #(parameter bit [3:0] N = 4)(...);               // narrower than int: N = 16 reads as 0

groups.title: Stage `imports`: the proof file
groups.intro: The checker builds only SvGolf, the task modules and the evaluator; a module outside the allowlist is unaudited code outside the trusted base. Mathlib and its packages (Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient) are on the allowlist. One solution file in v0.
groups.write_ok:
import Submission.Design
import LeanModels.Sv.Ingest2
import SvGolf.Comb
import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
groups.refused_example:
import Examples.python.tri.proof
import LeanModels.Python.Semantics
import Mathlib2.Tactic     -- a lookalike
import MyHelpers

groups.title: The trusted statement: interface, clocks, termination, function, range
groups.intro: The statement is a Lean `Prop` fixed by the task (`SvGolf/Task.lean`). A design that satisfies it must have exactly the task's ports, no edge-phase process, a completed run for every schedule and stimulus, and the task's function at every cycle, for every N in the range. These are not rules you can argue with: a design that breaks one has no proof of the statement, and the repository checks the refutations in `tests/*/negative/Refute.lean`.

groups.title: Stages `comparator`, `leanchecker`, `integrity`: the proof itself
groups.intro: The kernel must accept your theorem from the task's allowed axioms alone. Everything that would let a proof depend on something other than the kernel is refused.
groups.write_ok:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by
  -- induction on bit indices, decide +kernel for fixed-size subgoals
  ...
groups.refused_example:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by native_decide   -- trusts the compiler
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by sorry
axiom cheat : Submission.Goal

groups.title: Stages `score` and `postsynth`: the scored netlist
groups.intro: The score is area in NAND2 gate equivalents and depth, measured on the pinned Yosys + ABC netlist. The post-synthesis check then simulates ls-sv and the scored netlist on the task's vector budget and rejects any difference; it is sampling, so a difference confined to a tiny input region can slip through, which is what the static rules above are for. A rejection here is a bug report: either ls-sv or Yosys is wrong.
groups.refused_example: always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b;    // a flip-flop in the netlist: not priced

groups.title: Task authors: `task.json`
groups.intro: Mistakes in a task definition fail loudly so a typo cannot silently change the vector budget or the banlist.
groups.refused_example:
"banlist": {"operators": ["<<"]}     // unknown operator
"allow_bv_decide": true                  // an infrastructure error: no external solvers

never_summary: Anything the PIPELINE tools read differently (slang and ls-sv for the proof, Yosys for the score, Verilator and Xcelium as simulators; `P-NO-SILENT-PICK`, and `P-SAME-PROGRAM` where Yosys differs from slang): narrow net actuals into wider net inputs, partly out-of-range part selects, bit-select indexes wider than 32 bits, context-width port actuals, instance-parameter overrides evaluated at different widths, initialized variables with a second writer, the hex string escape `\xHH` (Yosys and Xcelium read the letter x; the named control escapes `\a \v \f` are admitted since 2026-11-01, Xcelium alone differs), self-reading `always_comb` (the event-driven simulators against the synthesizers). A difference that only Icarus (or only Xcelium, against LRM text the others follow) shows is a declared departure, not a refusal.

Programs slang rejects (`P-SAME-PROGRAM`; what the slang driver reports: parse and elaboration errors always, analysis errors too since 2026-11-01 (the banlist front check and the fourstate stage read them), with what is still unread listed under 'limits'): undeclared names, two writers of one bit when one of them is `always_comb`/`always_ff`, writing an input port, an undefined module, an `always` without timing control. Yosys alone would accept several of them silently.
Tool directives of any kind (`P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES`): `ifdef SYNTHESIS, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments.

Delays, timing and randomness in a combinational task (`P-NO-TIME`, `P-DETERMINISM`); non-hardware constructs such as classes, strings, reals, dynamic memory and `fork`/`join` (`P-SYNTHESIZABLE`: out of scope while the scored frontend is Yosys `read_verilog -sv`). Host access (reading files, system calls, DPI) is disallowed by its own policy (Thomas, 2026-10-31).
Anything that lets a submission change what the checker trusts (`P-TRUSTED-BASE`): `sorry`, user axioms, `extern` / `implemented_by`, a player-supplied envelope.

Anything in the SystemVerilog text that reaches the machine the checker runs on (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`; the Lean file is not covered, see the limits): `$readmemh` / `$readmemb` / `$writemem*`, `$fopen` and the file I/O family, `$system`, `$test$plusargs` / `$value$plusargs`, dump writers (`$dumpfile`, ...), DPI imports and exports, and escaped `$`-names that Yosys reads as system tasks.
lifting: Every refusal above has a state. `refused-now` means no change is planned. `later` names the prerequisite that has to exist first; when it exists, the refusal is lifted by a pull request.

**How to propose it.** Open a pull request against lean-surfaces that adds the feature to ls-sv (extractor, `LeanModels/Sv`), with differential cases against independent oracles (Xcelium pinned data, Icarus, Verilator, Yosys): a disagreement is fixed or declared, never ignored. Thomas approves every such PR.

**If the construct brings an x source** (a function local read before assignment, a latch that is never loaded, `always @*`), a rule in `score/fourstate.py` must land first or in the same PR; the post-synthesis check is the backstop, not the plan.

**For the checker's own rules** (the source gate, the banlist, the statement), changing a refusal changes what every earlier submission means: the PR must say so, and leaderboard entries record the lean-surfaces revision they were checked against.
**Update the register.** Add or edit the row in `docs/sv-refusals.json`, run `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --write`, and `--check` must pass.
limits: The post-synthesis check is sampling (fixed corners, task corners, harvested comparison constants, seeded random): a difference confined to a region no comparison constant selects can pass (`oob_rare.sv`, `zpair_add_rare.sv` pass it alone; the static rules are the only line there).

There is no sandbox: `import Lean` is allowed, so a Solution.lean can run `#eval` with checker privileges. The integrity snapshot is a tripwire, not a defence. Run untrusted submissions in a throwaway container. Measured (2026-10-31): a reference Solution.lean with an added `#eval IO.FS.readFile "/etc/hosts"` and an `IO.FS.writeFile` was ACCEPTED and did both, so the host-access refusals (`P-NO-HOST-ACCESS`) are a rule about the SystemVerilog text only.
Open (Thomas): should the Lean file be gated against host access too (`#eval`, `IO`, `run_cmd`, `elab`, `initialize`, `unsafe`; `import Lean` is allowed)? Nothing gates it today.

The parameter's declared type is not pinned by the statement; the multi-point cross-check at the scoring point keeps the scored design one ls-sv and slang agree on, elsewhere the statement is about ls-sv's reading.
The banlist front check is heuristic (a variable copied from a loop counter counts as run-time); the Yosys backstop covers the scored points only.

The fourstate stage checks the SCORING POINT only (not the probe points) and filters `tri-state` warnings out of Yosys `check`. Its run-time index rule reasons from index TYPES: `a[i-1]` with a 2-bit `i` is a 32-bit index and is refused on any declared range (over-refusal), as is any procedural loop counter used as an index.

A gate hole not yet measured: x/z digits are exempt anywhere inside a casez/casex item EXPRESSION, not only as the item's own literal (`casez (a[1:0]) (a[0] == 1'bz) ? 2'b00 : 2'b01: ...` passes the gate). Whether ls-sv and Yosys then differ was not measured; do not rely on it.

A plain syntax error is reported by the gate as `preprocessor-skipped text` before the extractor or Yosys see it; `always @(*)` passes the gate (the `(*)` is exempt) and is refused later by the language tier.
`ARITH_PRIMITIVES` (`$alu $macc $macc_v2 $lcu $fa`) in the banlist backstop are dead entries: the backstop reads without `-icells`, so instantiating one fails earlier with `yosys failed`.

`--no-gate` in `score.py` and `postsynth.py` is a research flag: the result says `gated: false` and is not a svGolf score. Missing Verilator, make, a C++ compiler, Yosys or `svgolf-eval` is an infrastructure error (exit 2), never a rejection.
Open policy question: comparisons are not banned in `add` / `mul`; a carry written as a comparison is Yosys's own alu logic and scores lower depth than the proved ripple reference.
Open: must challenge proofs be parametric (for all N)? The README treats it as decided; `svgolf/PLAN.md` still lists it as a question for Thomas.

slang's ANALYSIS-pass errors (`multiple-always-assigns`, `mixed-var-assigns`, `multiple-cont-assigns`, "cannot assign to input port", "'always' procedure does not advance time") are read since 2026-11-01 by the banlist front check and the `fourstate` stage (`score/slangdriver.py`, the Driver's own severities, per parameter point) and by the extractor. Still unread: the elaboration warnings the driver promotes to errors (`IndexOOB`, `RangeOOB`, ...: `fourstate`'s rule (c) refuses the out-of-range ones as x sources); a task with an EMPTY banlist skips the banlist front check, so `fourstate` is the only stage that reads them there; a module the design does not instantiate (docs/sv-refusals.json, `holes`).

Mathlib and the packages its import closure reaches (Batteries, Aesop, Qq, ProofWidgets, Plausible, ImportGraph, LeanSearchClient: the module roots, pinned by lean-surfaces' lake-manifest.json) ARE admitted since 2026-10-31 (Thomas): a proof that uses them is accepted on the same terms as any other, by the kernel from the task's allowed axioms alone. The comparator walks the dependency closure for axioms (a `native_decide` behind a Mathlib lemma is rejected like one in the file) and REPLAYS that closure, minus the toolchain and the submission's own modules, through the kernel, so a package olean whose declaration was added without kernel checking is rejected; toolchain modules must resolve into the toolchain; the integrity tripwire watches the Lean search path (`.olean` files of the packages, entries that do not exist) for every solution; the imports Lean recorded in the compiled solution are compared with the header the checker read.

entries.tag: ports that are not EXACTLY the task's (names, order, widths)
entries.trigger: an extra or hidden input (en, a rounding-mode pin); a renamed port (ci for cin); a wider or merged output; an inout
entries.why: Stimulus conventions ignore unknown names and store values at their own width, so only pinned ports mean what the hypothesis says.

entries.tag: any edge-phase process (always_ff, always @(posedge clk), an async-reset block), even with a dead clock
entries.trigger: always_ff @(posedge clk) s <= a ^ b;  clock tied low or undriven
entries.why: ls-sv runs every edge-phase process once per cycle whatever its clock holds, so a register on a clock nothing drives holds the right value in ls-sv and x in every simulator (0 GE in Yosys).
entries.prerequisite: the sequential layer: ls-sv models clock edges; the `Unclocked` requirement goes then
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: keep things combinatorial to begin with
entries.value_note: registered, pipelined and multi-cycle designs (serial multiplier, iterative divider)
entries.notes: Since WP-Q0 (2026-10-30) ls-sv itself refuses a dead, tied, gated, derived, register, internal-net, multiple or data-read clock and an internal asynchronous reset at the loader (gu-clock-source, gu-clock-reset, gu-clock-multiple, gu-clock-data-read in docs/sv-refusals.md), so a CLOCKED design that loads is single-clock and input-port-clocked. `Unclocked` stays the statement-level requirement of combinational tasks; the sequential statement (ClockedBy, svgolf/design/sequential/README.md) replaces it and the loader refusals are its loader-side twin.

entries.tag: a design that never settles or has no completed run (Terminates2)
entries.trigger: a combinational loop; a design the loader refused (errorDesign)
entries.why: Models2 quantifies over completed runs only, so a design that never settles satisfies every property vacuously; Terminates2 requires a completed run for every schedule and stimulus.

entries.tag: outputs that are not exactly the task's function at EVERY cycle with fully known inputs
entries.trigger: the wrong function; an output left x/z; correct only at the scoring point; outputs depending on earlier cycles
entries.why: The conjunct holds at every cycle of every run, whatever the earlier stimulus; a design cannot keep the hypothesis false by driving its own inputs.
entries.notes: The history clause becomes `later` with the sequential layer.

entries.tag: a clocked transaction that misses the frozen TxTask guarantee: done not within lat cycles of the start edge, or done and the payload not held at result x until the next accepted start or reset
entries.trigger: an off-by-one step counter; unsigned instead of signed products; a missing sign extension; done one cycle early; the accumulator not cleared on start; an accumulator truncated to 2W
entries.why: `TxTask.Statement` (txtask-v1, svgolf/SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean) claims `Guar` for every transaction under `Released` and `Rely`, at every parameter point in range, and the proof must establish it; a design wrong at any point, or late by a cycle, fails at the solution stage. Each matmul attack is also wrong at post-synthesis (`check.py --unproved`), so none is merely different.

entries.tag: a clocked stream that misses the frozen StreamTask guarantee: out_valid unknown or raised before the first start, or a transaction's out_valid cycles not emitting exactly spec xs (the input sorted ascending, duplicates kept) within lat cycles of the start edge
entries.trigger: the token shift reading the cell's own token (no value ever emitted); a missing else (two writes, the later wins); the neighbour push comparing the cell's own value; the valid token entering with the start (out_valid one cycle early, one value too many); a reset that leaves the cells; a top cell the drain does not clear; signed instead of unsigned order
entries.why: `StreamTask.Statement` (txtask-v1, svgolf/SvGolf/TaskSeq.lean) claims `Guar` for every transaction under `Released` and `Rely`, at every parameter point in range, and the proof must establish it; a design wrong at any point, or one value early or late, fails at the solution stage. Each sorter attack is also wrong at post-synthesis (`check.py --unproved`), so none is merely different; designs that differ from the reference only in how they order EQUAL values (`>=` for `>`) are not attacks, since equal values are interchangeable in the emitted list.

entries.trigger: theorem t : ... := by sorry; also a goal ADMITTED by a tactic after it logged an error (the WP-G tactic elaborators log their refusal and admit the goal, so the proof compiles with an error and depends on sorryAx)

entries.trigger: theorem t : ... := by native_decide
entries.why: native_decide trusts the compiled evaluator, not the kernel: it adds a per-declaration axiom `<decl>._native.native_decide.ax_1_1` that no static allow list can name.
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-27 (svGolf decision: native_decide stays banned)
entries.notes: TENSION to confirm: AGENTS.md records Thomas's 2026-08-22 ruling that native_decide / bv_decide are not banned, only discouraged, for the lean-surfaces proof lanes; svGolf has no per-task escape.

entries.trigger: theorem t : ... := by bv_decide;  task.json allow_bv_decide: true
entries.why: bv_decide runs an external SAT solver (the toolchain's `cadical`), and the checker does not support external solvers (Thomas 2026-11-01: "Let's not support external solvers for now"). Supporting it needs the solution's compile sandbox to grant `fork`, the exec of `cadical` and a writable temporary directory (measured: all three), which also lets a hostile file start further copies of `lean`. Without the grant the tactic fails in the sandbox with `operation not permitted` (check.py adds a hint at `solution`); with --sandbox off the comparator rejects the generated axiom `<decl>._native.bv_decide.ax_*`, naming the policy; `allow_bv_decide: true` is an infrastructure error. The comparator's re-verification of the axiom and the sandbox grant are kept, dormant, behind the constant `BV_DECIDE_SUPPORTED` in check.py.
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-11-01, after the sandbox widening was explained to him ("maybe that's a bad idea. Let's not support external solvers for now")
entries.evidence: svgolf/README.md "`bv_decide`"; svgolf/design/bv-decide/NOTE.md; svgolf/tests/checker/test_import_packages.py BvDecideFlag; svgolf/tests/checker/test_bv_decide.py; tests/run.py attacks bv_decide_shaped, bv_decide_subgoal_sandbox, bv_decide_subgoal_off (and the groundwork rows)

Since WP-C3 the `design` stage rejects the loaded envelope that carries the Unsupported node (`Design2.hasUnsupported`); the postsynth stage, alone, still fails closed on it. Both lines hold today.
